claim.text: Encounter item whose "you" addressee is not resolved by the packet: terminology could refer to the respondent or the interviewer, so the report grain cannot be fixed; only if administration is interviewer-delivered would it describe representatives approaching the interviewer during field contact rather than the respondent's own political contact, and no such design assumption is made here.

evidence.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?

changed_claims.previous_text: Interviewer-reported dyadic exposure: the interviewer discloses whether community or political-party representatives approached the interviewer (not the respondent) in connection with this fieldwork visit, so the observation is an interviewer's encounter with external mobilizers, not the respondent's own political contact.

claim.text: Felt-threat item using "you" without an identified addressee; it records a felt state during the interview whose reporter grain the packet does not settle, and it is not an observed physical act.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?

changed_claims.previous_text: Affective threat is reported by the interviewer about the interviewer's own feeling during the interview; it records a felt state at interviewer grain, not an observed act or the respondent's fear.

claim.text: Physical-threat item distinct in stem from the felt-threat question; the packet supplies no relationship, nesting, or co-occurrence result, so a 'No' here is not asserted to negate a 'Yes' on felt threat.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

changed_claims.previous_text: Physically threatened is a distinct interviewer-side claim of bodily threat; it is separable from felt threat and from mere disruption, so a 'No' here does not negate a 'Yes' on felt threat.

changed_claims.previous_text: Interviewer's retrospective characterization of the respondent's candor; the middle option is an explicit uncommitted judgment, not a mild version of adversarial candor, and refusal/don't-know are absent by design.

changed_inquiries.question: Only if interviewer identity and any clustering are verified, and only if the threat items' unverified addressee and Q97's unverified administration are qualified: does co-variation between a felt or physical threat report and the respondent's attributed sponsorship distinguish a pressure environment from misattribution or random interviewer distress?
changed_inquiries.alternatives: If sponsor attribution and threat reports were shown to co-vary after interviewer identity and clustering are verified, that pattern would be consistent with (but not establish) an environment-of-pressure reading; flatness across sponsor categories, or concentration among Afrobarometer-attributors, would count against the pressure interpretation. The cross-sectional packet cannot adjudicate between these.
changed_inquiries.ceiling: Candidate hypothesis only: source route, design, and roles must be qualified first; interviewer identity and clustering, the addressee of the threat items, and actual Q97 administration are all unverified here; no numerics are asserted and nothing establishes intimidation causation.
changed_inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.

changed_inquiries.question: Prerequisite: all three items (Q50B, Q51A, Q51B) must be verified as administered to the same respondents with linkage established before any cross-item comparison; given that, does anticipated harassment of a woman candidate co-occur with a different women's-rights priority and a different demand direction than a general-expansion stance, i.e., are hostile-environment perceivers more likely to name gender-based violence and demand more government action than those who expect little sanction?
changed_inquiries.alternatives: If high anticipated sanction pairs with gender-based-violence priority and more-government demand, this supports a threat-to-priority linkage; if high-sanction respondents name structural issues (pay, property) or prefer the status quo, the sanction-expectation and policy-preference accounts are rival readings; without verified same-respondent administration and linkage of all three items, no pairing is interpreted.
changed_inquiries.ceiling: Cross-sectional metadata only; all three item administration and same-respondent linkage are a prerequisite, not established by this packet; priority is capped-choice so nonselection does not imply low importance, and nothing establishes that expectations cause demand.
changed_inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.

changed_inquiries.question: Only if same-wave co-administration of Q48A with Q48B, and of Q28 with Q29B, is verified: do respondents who assign legislative oversight to the executive also endorse presidential non-bindingness or conditional military takeover, indicating an executive-centered accountability frame, or do the items dissociate?
changed_inquiries.alternatives: A coherent executive-centered configuration would be consistent with a single frame; dissociation would show that owner designation about MPs is not a proxy for authoritarian legality. Because joint administration and same-respondent linkage are unverified, neither pattern is currently established.
changed_inquiries.ceiling: Candidate hypothesis only: owner targets (MPs vs president) stay separate and Q48A's Burkina Faso date code bars same-respondent use unless co-administration is verified; no causal inference and no claim that owner answers predict behavior or that the four items share a denominator.
changed_inquiries.route: S04 existing observation-scope and asked-eligible RAW owner; only after source route, design and roles qualified.

existing_holds.why: A same-respondent comparison of presidential versus legislative oversight attribution presupposes joint administration that this metadata does not establish.
